title: The Operational Facilitator can accelerate an Artifact edit in an emergency and may withhold the announcement
content:
A.6.1.1.5.2.2.2.2.1.2.3.1 provides that in an Emergency Situation as defined by the Sky Core Atlas, "the Operational Facilitator **may allow a Root Edit to occur more quickly** than the timeline specified above. Where feasible, the Operational Facilitator should announce the decision to deploy the emergency Root Edit protocol and provide their reasoning via a public Sky Forum post … **unless doing so would endanger Obex or its users**."

Three discretions stack in one sentence. The Facilitator decides whether the emergency protocol applies, decides how much of the timeline to compress, and decides whether announcing it is safe. The announcement duty is further softened by "should" rather than "must," and qualified by "where feasible" before the endangerment carve-out is even reached.

The carve-out is nonetheless well motivated. Publicising that governance safeguards are being bypassed can itself be the exploitable event — an attacker learns both that a vulnerability exists and that normal review is suspended. Silence is sometimes the only safe path.

What is absent is the compensating control such a power usually carries: no maximum compression, no post-hoc ratification vote, no deadline for delayed disclosure once the danger passes, and no external confirmation that a genuine Emergency Situation existed. The definition of an emergency is at least externalised to the Atlas (A.1.9.1.1), which keeps the trigger from being self-defined — but the response remains a single actor's judgement. This is worth flagging as the sharpest concentration of unilateral power in Obex's governance.
description: Emergency Root Edits compress the normal timeline at the Facilitator's discretion, with public disclosure required only "where feasible" and excused if it would endanger Obex or its users.
